seoTitle: Free Caddyfile Generator for Common Sites
metaDescription: Free online Caddyfile generator. Build a site block for reverse proxy, static files, SPA, PHP-FPM or redirect with compression, headers and www redirect.
intro: Build a Caddyfile site block for a reverse proxy, static file server, single-page app, PHP-FPM site or redirect, with compression, security headers, logging and an optional www redirect.
why:
Caddy is popular because it gets HTTPS certificates automatically and has a short configuration language. Even so, the common recipes are easy to forget: how a single-page app falls back to index.html, how to hand PHP to FPM, or which security headers to add.

Enter the site address and choose a mode. Reverse proxy takes an upstream such as localhost:3000, file server and SPA take a root folder, PHP uses php_fastcgi with a socket path you should check, and redirect takes a target URL. You can add encode zstd gzip, a header block, access logging, tls internal for local certificates and a global ACME email. The headers are sensible defaults, not a full security policy. Nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Enter the site address, for example example.com.
Choose a mode and enter the upstream, root folder or redirect target.
Tick compression, security headers, logging and www redirect as needed.
Copy the Caddyfile, then run caddy validate and reload.

faq.a: Yes, for public domain names, Caddy obtains and renews certificates by itself. Use tls internal for local names, where it issues certificates from its own authority instead.

faq.q: How does the SPA mode work?
faq.a: It serves files from the root folder and uses try_files to fall back to /index.html for unknown paths, so client-side routes work when someone reloads the page.

faq.q: Is the PHP socket path correct for my system?
faq.a: The tool uses unix//run/php/php-fpm.sock as a common default. Package names and versions vary, so confirm the real socket path on your server.

faq.q: What does the www redirect do?
faq.a: It adds a second site block for www.yourdomain that redirects permanently to the bare domain, keeping the path and query.
